meta.title: ChiShona Grade 7 - Original Practice Set
meta.note: All items below were freshly written for this practice set. Traditional proverbs (tsumo) and totems (mitupo) are general Shona folklore/cultural knowledge in the public domain; the specific selection, wording of explanations, and question format here are original and not copied from any published revision guide.

tsumo_practice.instructions: Complete each tsumo, then check the meaning given.

items.meaning: Unity brings strength; one person alone struggles to achieve what a group can achieve together.
Dishonesty eventually destroys a relationship or reputation.
Kindness given is usually returned in kind.
A leader or elder should set an example of humility so that younger ones can follow.
A taboo is not something that respects itself; it is people who must respect and observe it.
One person cannot surround or accomplish a big task alone; teamwork is needed.
If you do not speak up about a problem, it may never be solved.
There are things kept hidden or secret within a household that outsiders do not see.
The one who caused harm may forget, but the one who suffered it often remembers.
Kinship alone is not complete without generosity and sharing.

madimikira_practice.instructions: Match each idiom to its meaning.

items.meaning: to complain about something out of one's control / to be extremely angry with no clear target
to secretly harbour a dangerous grudge or enemy
to refuse to listen or take advice
to be in extreme pain or shock

nyaudzosingwi_practice.instructions: Choose the ideophone that best completes each sentence.

ukama_quiz.instructions: Choose the correct kinship term for each description.

items.question: What do you call your father's older brother?
What do you call your mother's brother?
What is a man's sister's child called to him?
What do you call your spouse's younger sibling (opposite sex)?
What is a grandfather's father called?

mitupo_practice.instructions: Match the totem (mutupo) to its chidau (praise name) - pairs are widely known Shona cultural knowledge.

sample_composition_prompts.instructions: Original prompts for practising rondedzero, tsamba and hurukuro writing (approx. 120 words each).

items.prompt: Nyora rondedzero pamusoro pezuva rako rekuzvarwa rakaipa rawakambosangana naro.
Nyora tsamba kushamwari yako uchiitaurira nezverwendo rwawakaita kunze kwenyika.
Nyora hurukuro pakati pababa nemwana vachikurukura pamusoro pekukosha kwedzidzo.
Nyora mhan'arwa kumukuru wechikoro pamusoro perutivi rwechikoro rwakakuvadzwa nedutu.
